In his 1597 music textbook, Morley said balletts, also called fa las, were songs for dancing as well as singing, and that the first set he had seen was by the Italian Gastoldi.

source.en: Thomas Morley, A Plaine and Easie Introduction to Practicall Musicke (1597), excerpt "Thomas Morley on Kinds of Vocal Music", University of Mississippi course page

Earlier English editors put English words to unchanged Italian pieces. For his 1595 balletts, Morley instead wrote new music loosely modeled on Italian ones.

source.en: Megan Kaes Long, "Characteristic Tonality in the Balletti of Gastoldi, Morley, and Hassler", Journal of Music Theory (abstract), Oberlin College Digital Commons
